answer: A sponsor-backed graduated trust system resists sybils: a new agent joins only if an established operator stakes a bond on it, slashed if the newcomer cheats. The newcomer starts behind a ridge of low limits — tiny jobs and capped payments — and climbs only after verified successful work. A fable of many fakes fails because each needs its own stake and slow climb, while a juniper cutting beside the real path is easy to spot: identical patterns across supposedly independent agents trigger audit and collective slashing, making forgery costlier than honest work.
